raw_comment: The drought map highlights the rarity and severity of current conditions across the United States. Exceptional drought (D4) occurs in less than 2% of historical conditions, making it extremely rare, while extreme drought (D3) reflects conditions in the 2nd to 5th percentiles. In regions like the Midwest, where D3-D4 levels dominate, drought indicators such as precipitation and soil moisture are alarmingly low, underscoring the severity. Approximately 10% of the U.S. is in exceptional drought, while larger portions are experiencing extreme, severe, or moderate drought, with only Alaska and Kentucky remaining unaffected.
